summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary Box
summaryBox.takeaway: Consumer protists include saprophytic slime molds and phagotrophic protozoans. Paramecium exhibits nuclear dimorphism. Plasmodium alternates between human schizogony and mosquito sporogony.

conceptBreakdown.content: Consumer protists encompass saprophytic slime molds and animal-like heterotrophic protozoans adapted to predatory or parasitic modes of life.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Slime Molds (Fungus-like Protists / Mycetozoa)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Slime Molds (Fungus-like Protists / Mycetozoa)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Slime molds are saprophytic protists that move along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic matter.

A. Acellular / Plasmodial Slime Molds (Myxomycetes):
• Vegetative Phase: Under favorable conditions, forms a free-living, multinucleate, wall-less mass of protoplasm called a Plasmodium (coenocytic diploid mass).
• Reproductive Phase: Under unfavorable conditions (starvation/desiccation), the plasmodium differentiates into erect fruiting bodies (Sporangia). Sporangia contain a network of threads called Capillitium that aid in spore dispersal. Spores possess true, highly resistant cell walls composed of cellulose.

B. Cellular Slime Molds (Dictyosteliomycetes):
• Vegetative Phase: Consists of individual haploid uninucleate amoeboid cells (myxamoebae).
• Aggregation: Upon starvation, myxamoebae secrete cyclic AMP (cAMP) as a chemotactic signal to aggregate into a multicellular migratory 'slug' (Pseudoplasmodium), forming a fruiting body (sorocarp) without cell fusion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Protozoans (Animal-Like Protists)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Protozoans (Animal-Like Protists)
conceptBreakdown.content:
All protozoans are heterotrophs (predators or parasites). Divided into four major functional groups based on locomotory organelles:

1. Amoeboid Protozoans:
• Move and capture prey by extending pseudopodia (false feet) driven by actin-myosin streaming (e.g., *Amoeba proteus*).
• Marine forms (*Foraminifera* and *Radiolaria*) possess shells of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) or silica (SiO2).
• Parasitic species: *Entamoeba histolytica* (causes amoebic dysentery; lacks mitochondria, possesses mitosomes).

2. Flagellated Protozoans:
• Propelled by flagella. Parasitic taxa include:
- *Trypanosoma brucei*: Transmitted by Tsetse fly (*Glossina*); causes African Sleeping Sickness. Exhibits antigenic variation of its Variant Surface Glycoprotein (VSG) coat.
- *Leishmania donovani*: Transmitted by Sandfly (*Phlebotomus*); causes Kala-azar (Visceral Leishmaniasis).
- *Trichomonas vaginalis*: Causes trichomoniasis.

3. Ciliated Protozoans (e.g., Paramecium caudatum):
• Possess thousands of coordinated cilia and a permanent cell mouth (cytostome) opening into the gullet.
• Nuclear Dimorphism: Contains two distinct nuclei:
  - Macronucleus: Polyploid; controls somatic vegetative metabolism.
  - Micronucleus: Diploid; controls sexual reproduction (Conjugation).
• Defensively deploy explosive extrusible organelles called Trichocysts.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Sporozoans & The Plasmodium Life Cycle
conceptBreakdown.title: Sporozoans & The Plasmodium Life Cycle
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PLASMODIUM LIFE CYCLE
                        
       HUMAN HOST (Intermediate Host)         ANOPHELES MOSQUITO (Definitive Host)
       [Asexual Cycle / Schizogony]             [Sexual Cycle / Sporogony]
       
  Anopheles Bite (Injects SPOROZOITES)             Gametocytes Ingested in Blood Meal
              │                                                 │
              ▼                                                 ▼
   Hepatocytes (Exo-erythrocytic)                    Syngamy in Mosquito Midgut
              │                                    (Ookinete ──► Oocyst)
              ▼                                                 │
   Erythrocytes (Erythrocytic Cycle)                            ▼
   (Trophozoite ──► Schizont ──► Merozoites)         Sporogony Produces SPOROZOITES
              │                                    (Migrate to Salivary Glands)
              ▼
   Release of Hemozoin Toxin (Causes Fever) ──► Gametocytes Formed
conceptBreakdown.content:
Sporozoans (*Plasmodium vivax*, *P. falciparum*) are obligate endoparasites characterized by an infectious spore-like stage, absence of locomotory organelles, and an Apical Complex (rhoptries/micronemes) for host erythrocyte penetration.

• Human Phase (Intermediate Host - Asexual Schizogony):
- Mosquito bite injects sporozoites into blood.
- Liver hepatocytes undergo exo-erythrocytic schizogony.
- Erythrocytic schizogony: Trophozoites feed on hemoglobin, producing toxic Hemozoin crystals that trigger cyclical chills and high fever when RBCs rupture.
- Gametocytes form in human blood.

• Mosquito Phase (Definitive Host - Sexual Sporogony):
- Female *Anopheles* ingests gametocytes in blood meal.
- Syngamy occurs in mosquito midgut, forming a motile Ookinete and encysted Oocyst.
- Sporogony generates thousands of infective sporozoites that migrate to the salivary glands.
